question.text: The trajectory of an object follows the path y = x²/2, with its horizontal position changing over time according to x = t²/2 (where x and y are given in metres and t is given in seconds). Find the velocity vector of this object at the instant t = 2 s (in m s⁻¹).
conditions: coordinates x and y are in metres

solution.approach: Write x and y separately as functions of time, differentiate each with respect to time, and evaluate both at t = 2 s.

steps.text: Write x as a function of t and differentiate to get the x-component of velocity.
Write y in terms of t by substituting x = t²/2 into y = x²/2.
Differentiate y with respect to t to get the y-component of velocity.
Evaluate both components at t = 2 s.
Write the velocity vector at t = 2 s.

common_mistakes.text: Swapping which component is which, writing vₓ = 4 and v_y = 2 instead of vₓ = 2 and v_y = 4.
